short: A decisive Italian victory that shattered the Austro-Hungarian army and led directly to the empire's collapse and surrender.
full:
On 24 October 1918, exactly a year after the disaster at Caporetto, the Italian army launched a massive offensive across the Piave river against the Austro-Hungarian forces. After days of fierce resistance, the Austro-Hungarian lines broke at the town of Vittorio Veneto, splitting their army in two. As mutinies spread and the empire at home began to disintegrate into independent states, the Austro-Hungarian military collapsed entirely.

The Italian advance rapidly turned into a pursuit, capturing hundreds of thousands of prisoners and vast quantities of materiel. The overwhelming victory forced Austria-Hungary to sign the Armistice of Villa Giusti on 3 November 1918, knocking Germany's primary ally out of the war and accelerating the end of the global conflict.
